Raj (runtime): saw a p99 blip in prod during a customer burst, ~350ms higher than baseline for NVidia T4 pool. attaching quick profile.
Maya (perf): ugh, is this the cold-KV scenario or kernel fallback?
Raj (runtime): looks like both. kernel selector probed fallback matmul on some requests (~seq<=64), but the big delta lines up with KV misses during scale-up.
Liam: can you paste the flame output? also which microbatch config on that host?
Raj (runtime): flame svg: /var/log/profiles/1954001234/p99-flame.svg
Raj (runtime): microbatch config was dynamic: target_batch_ms=15, max_batch=8, aggressive_backoff=true
Sophia: that backoff + small max_batch is likely hurting throughput when burst queues up -> more scale events.
Maya (perf): profiling snippet: 70% of extra time is in KV fetch + kernel recompile fallback cost (~8-12ms per request accumulative). we saw kernel selector fall back to scalar matmul for ~18% of calls during the probe window.
Raj (runtime): exact log: "kernel_probe: chosen=matmul_v1 fallback=matmul_scalar reason=latency_spike" — repeated at 1.5s intervals because prober sampled too often.
Liam: prober sampling frequency + autoscaler cadence interplay here. prober forced kernel churn while autoscaler spun up new pods which didn't have warmed KV caches.
Sophia: autoscaler lag was ~20s. during that time new replicas got requests but KV cold-read penalty is ~40ms on average (disk-backed K/V shard). combined with kernel fallback makes tail bad.
Maya (perf): quick mitigation ideas: 1) lower prober sampling in burst windows, 2) increase microbatch target to 30ms for hosts hitting >100qps to amortize KV penalty, 3) prewarm KV on new replica init if coming from autoscaler event.
Raj (runtime): also thinking of asymmetric microbatch: prefer slightly larger batch for short seq to hide KV jitter, but keep p50 latency SLO. we can tune p95 target with a soft error budget.
Liam: is there telemetry to detect when prober is causing regressions? we could compare per-kernel p99 delta and auto-disable prober for a host if delta>10ms for 30s.
Maya (perf): yes, add a prober-health metric: kernel_probe_delta_p99 and disable if above threshold. also add KV-warmup hook: when replica registers for traffic, do a small synthetic request to populate local cache for top N prefixes.
Sophia: one more: change autoscaler burst policy to prefer burst capacity on existing nodes (burst-capacity pool) instead of immediate scale-up to new cold reps. that reduces cold-KV impact.
Raj (runtime): I'll draft an experiment: adjust prober rate from 1/s -> 1/6s during high-load, microbatch target 15->30ms for bursty hosts, and enable KV prewarm synthetic for new replicas. roll canary to 10% of T4 pool.
perf-bot: canary rollout created: prober-tune/experiment-1954001234 -> 10% (ID: cr-1954001234)
Liam: cool. include the test plan: measure p50/p95/p99 and kernel-change-rate. also verify token throughput doesn't regress >3%.
Maya (perf): I'll add synthetic workload matching the customer's request mix and run overnight. collecting traces for 24h.
Raj (runtime): thanks, will post results in thread when we have numbers. initial guess is p99 should drop by ~120ms for that segment.
Sophia: if the canary looks good, let's add an autoscaler heuristic: prefer warm-host routing for the first 30s of a burst.
Raj (runtime): noted. creating GH issue with experiment details.
Liam: thx — ping me on the GH so I can help with the prewarm implementation.
Maya (perf): tagging perf dashboards too. :rocket:
perf-bot: perf-metric alert cleared for pool:t4-prod (incident 9876 resolved)"
